questions.question: What does continuity at $x_0$ require in the metric-space definition?
options: There exists a single $\varepsilon \gt 0$ such that for every $\delta \gt 0$, $d_Y(f(x),f(x_0)) \lt \varepsilon$
For every $\varepsilon \gt 0$, there exists $0 \lt \delta\leq r$ such that $d_X(x,x_0) \lt \delta$ implies $d_Y(f(x),f(x_0)) \lt \varepsilon$
The function must be linear on $E$

questions.question: Why does the definition assume there is an $r \gt 0$ with $B_X(x_0,r)\subseteq E$?
options: So the codomain $Y$ must be bounded
So points near $x_0$ lie in the domain $E$

questions.question: When is a vector-valued function continuous?
options: Only when at least one component is continuous
If and only if each component function is continuous

questions.question: Which operation is preserving continuity for real-valued functions of one real variable?
options: Division by a function that may be zero anywhere
Changing the domain metric without checking anything

questions.question: Which missing condition would make a continuity claim about a quotient unsafe?

There must be a ball around $x_0$ contained in $E$
